newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREAN WON ENDS HIGHER ON STRONGER YEN VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREAN WON ENDS HIGHER ON STRONGER YEN VS DOLLAR.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Thursday as the U.S. currency weakened versus the yen in Tokyo, dealers said.

They said announcement of Japan's June current account on Friday and possible trade disputes between Tokyo and Washington would decide the future market direction in the won/dollar market, which usually moves in line with the yen/dollar.
The won closed at 892.80, comparing with Wednesday's close of 893.00. It briefly hit a monthly low of 893.50 on a government procurement deal and some importer deals, dealers said.
The won mostly moved in a 892 won level after the dollar was quoted at 118.40-60 yen level.
"If the dollar climbs over 119 yen level, the greenback could rise to the 894 won level," said a dealer. "But the prospect looks unlikely."
Friday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 892.80 from 892.60 today.
